view.name: Adversarial Security & Usability
view.description: Runs adversarial passes on product docs and code for security and usability. Uses peer-agent tickets, operator-safe scripts, and honest live captures — not overclaimed mockups.

memory.content: Operator entrypoints should be foolproof: one command; the script checks prior instance terminated, git is current, cwd/env are right; the operator does not decide. Prefer a safety tapback when that preflight motif applies, and a refuse tapback when a dirty start is blocked.

Peer-agent ticket inbox convention: write each ticket as ~/reports/tickets/ticket-*.md (never drop tickets next to scratch adversarial reports at the reports root). Peer agent sweeps on pulse or when nudged about a new ticket. Tickets are proposals the peer may push back on. Never write adversarial reports or tickets into the product repo docs/ folder (pollutes clone checkouts).
Agent and peer-agent scratch reports belong under ~/reports/, not under the product repository docs/, so checkouts stay clean.

Local-only sequential drill when remote CI must stay quiet: checkout a branch from local main, implement, run the full local gate suite green, fast-forward merge into local main, delete the stale branch; never push origin/main. Durability mirrors go only to backup/* refs that do not trigger CI.

Full local build drill for each residue: write a deep decided ADR from the feature description (smart, striking, vivid product choices — not open ors) → adversarial pass on the ADR → implement on a local branch → adversarial pass on the code → full gates green → FF local main → delete stale branch; then auto-pick the next residue. Only stop to ask when blocked on a real product decision.

Config and product validation must use real loaders and real gates — never a TypeScript mirror of the source of truth. Prefer guided wiring over a free canvas. Honesty doctrine: do not overclaim; do not rebuild rejected field-level visibility designs without an explicit product ADR.

Standing image-ticket convention with a peer agent that lacks a generator: any visual ask is ~/reports/tickets/ticket-image-<slug>-<YYYY-MM-DD>.md with per-image id, screen/subject, size/aspect, highlight/edit notes, and output filename. This Bot generates or captures with no back-and-forth, drops finished files under ~/reports/, and the peer swaps them into the deliverable. Prefer live product captures over generated mockups when the brief requires honesty.

When a peer agent asks for images via the ticket inbox, generate or capture and drop them under ~/reports/. The peer is not a Grok teammate — async is filesystem tickets and handoffs, not agent-to-agent chat.
